note: Long-form craft findings and bugs, ranked. Written by Scout; the improver applies recipe, scene and design items, Studio follows script items.

items.title: Add a loan_prepay maths kind (reduce EMI vs reduce tenure, and tenure after a rate rise)
items.detail: renderer/models/maths.py has emi with a fixed months count, so no long video can show 'the loan ends N months earlier' or 'the tenure stretched by N months'. Add kind loan_prepay: inputs amount, rate_pct, months, prepay, prepay_month (and optional new_rate_pct). Values/figures: emi, interest_base, interest_reduce_emi, emi_reduced, months_reduce_tenure (closed form n = -ln(1 - rB/P)/ln(1+r) on the balance B at prepay_month), interest_reduce_tenure, saved_* for both, plus a balance series for the chart. Recompute independently in the number check. Unblocks topics 2026-10-18-prepay-emi-or-tenure and the tenure half of 2026-10-18-repo-hike-your-emi. Done when a checked example script uses it and number-check passes.

items.title: Add a sip_stepup maths kind (SIP raised by X% every year)
items.detail: Feed topic 2026-10-16-sip-stepup (priority high) and 2026-10-18-lifestyle-inflation both need a yearly step-up, which the sip kind cannot express. Add kind sip_stepup: monthly, step_pct, rate_pct, years; values final, invested, gains, final_flat (same start, no step-up) and a yearly series for both, for the chart scene's series/series2. Closed form per year (sum of yearly annuity blocks), recomputed independently in the number check. Done when a checked example script renders the two-line chart in stills.

items.title: End each chapter with a one-line recap card holding its key figure
items.detail: Teacher-style channels (CA Rachana Ranade's long videos) keep viewers through long explanations by closing each section with the one thing to remember. In long_story scripts, make the last beat of each chapter a bignumber with a kicker line 'So far' and the chapter's one computed figure, 3-4 s, before the next chapter card. A/B via a script flag so improvement.evaluate can compare average % viewed at chapter boundaries. Works if retention dips at chapter cards shrink in the experiment arm.

items.title: Open long videos on a concrete moment the viewer has lived (an SMS, a payslip, an app button)
items.detail: The channels that win long-form here (Labour Law Advisor's mis-selling and EPF videos, this week's repo/EMI videos) open on the viewer's own situation, not on a concept. In the first beat of every long_story script, put a cast member in one recognisable moment (bank SMS 'rate revised', appraisal letter, the prepay button in the app) with the rupee stake as a computed figure on screen within 5 s; the concept explanation comes after the first chapter card. Studio applies it when writing; check it in the Saturday review of the first 30 s.

items.title: New scene: an 'inputs' form that fills itself in before a calculation
items.detail: Calculator-led channels (Asset Yogi's spreadsheet walk-throughs) earn trust by showing the inputs before the answer. We have no scene for that: add an inputs scene to remotion/src/scenes showing 3-4 labelled fields (amount, rate, years, step-up) typing in one by one from the beat's maths figures, with an 'assumption' tag on the rate, then handing off to split/chart. All values come from the timeline figures, never typed. Behind a flag; look at it in stills first. Works if it passes the layout probe and liveliness, and % viewed holds through the setup beats in the experiment arm.

items.title: Feed topics named a removed template (long_explainer)
items.detail: The four 2026-10-16 topics listed templates ['long_explainer'], which was removed with the Pillow engine; the only long template is long_story. Fixed today in improvement/longform/topics.json (Scout's file). If generator.run state matches topics by template, check it ignores unknown names rather than silently dropping topics. No action needed unless that check fails.

items.title: check-plan demands #Shorts on long videos
items.detail: generator/run.py check_plan fails every plan without #Shorts, including format long (L-20261018-01). A landscape 4-minute video should not carry #Shorts. Studio shipped without it (ship does not need the planner step). Fix: apply the rule only when plan_format(plan) == 'short', and add a test.

items.title: reveal/bignumber centre text runs under an actor at x 0.86
items.detail: QA on L-20261018-01 (beat future-self, ~127 s): the hero line 'paid by future Rohan' ran under Rohan, hiding the last word; the layout probe did not flag it. Fix in the scene: limit the text column to the area clear of the actor, or let the probe treat actors as obstacles. Studio worked around it by dropping the actor.

items.title: A stage opening needs its stake on screen from frame one
items.detail: QA failed L-20261018-01's first render: a stage beat (Rohan reading the bank SMS) showed no text until 3.5 s. Fixed with a chip at 'start' carrying the computed interest jump. Script rule for Studio: when the first beat is a stage moment, its chip (or a reveal line) shows a computed figure at 'start'. QA still calls a chip weaker than a big number; a bigger hook card over a stage scene would be a scene item.

items.title: Say the video's promise in one line between 20 and 30 seconds
items.detail: Retention guides agree on three beats for the first 30 s: prove the title with one concrete example (0-10 s), say why it matters to the viewer (10-20 s), then a one-line roadmap of what they will know by the end (20-30 s), repeating the title's number if it has one. Our first long video (L-20261018-01) does the first two well (bank SMS, then the interest stake in beat 2) but beat 4 ends on 'Let's find out why', which promises nothing specific. Studio: make the 3rd-4th beat a promise line naming two or three things the viewer will know (e.g. 'how long, how much, and the one number on your statement that fixes it'). No greeting, no channel intro, no full table of contents. How we know: first-30-second retention in YouTube Studio once long videos have views; until then, check every long script has such a line before 30 s.

items.title: End each chapter with a one-line tease of the next one (open loop)
items.detail: Explainer retention advice: open a loop every 2-3 minutes by teasing the next part before it starts ('and that was the good year'), and close the main question only in the last fifth. Build it as a flag `long_chapter_tease`: in the variant, Studio writes a tease line as the last beat before each `chapter` beat, and the chapter card shows it as its subtitle for the first second. Control: chapters as now. Pairs with, but is separate from, the 2026-10-18 recap-card experiment (recap looks back, tease looks forward); don't run both in the same video. Decide on % viewed per long video with improvement.evaluate.

items.title: Put the biggest reveal about two thirds of the way in, not at the end
items.detail: Saving the best figure for the finale loses the viewers who leave before it; guides put the best moment at about two thirds of the runtime and keep the end for the 'what to do' and recap. Studio: when ordering chapters, place the side-by-side or gap reveal (the video's biggest computed number) at 60-70% of the planned length. The four new 2026-10-19 topic outlines already mark where it goes. How we know: the reveal beat's start / duration_sec in render.json lands between 0.6 and 0.7.

items.title: card_min_due's docstring tells the writer the video mentions GST, wrong for US/UK cards
items.detail: renderer/models/maths.py card_min_due says real cards 'add GST on interest and fees ... The video says so'. GST is Indian; since the channel went global (2026-10-18) a USD card story must not say GST. Improver: change the docstring to 'taxes or fees on interest where they apply (GST in India)' and, if long_story/README.md or short_story/README.md repeat the GST line for card stories, make it country-aware. How we know: no non-INR script mentions GST.

items.title: A stage chip set 'at: start' is not visible on frame 0
items.detail: QA failed L-20261019-01's first render: the opening stage beat's chip ('Minimum due: $150', at: start) animates in after frame 0, so the first frame showed only Rohan in a room. bignumber/reveal lines at start are already drawn on frame 0 (data.tsx Lines: p.beat.from === 0 && start < 0.05). Improver: give the stage Chip the same frame-0 rule. Until then Studio opens on a bignumber with plain-text start lines (no value, which counts up from zero) and the actor beside them. This supersedes the 2026-10-18-first-frame-hook workaround.

items.title: camera push on a screen beat zooms its title out of the frame
items.detail: L-20261019-01's first render failed the layout gate ('Minimum only' outside the frame at 109 s): the screen scene's title sits at the top of the wall screen and the push camera scales the frame 1.09x. Fixed by using drift. Improver: keep screen content inside the push-safe area, or have the camera clamp scale for scenes with a top caption. Script rule for Studio meanwhile: no push on screen beats with a title.

items.title: A trailer Short can be blocked by the Shorts category window
items.detail: The trailer for L-20261019-01 (credit_card) failed check-plan twice: credit_card was used by v-20261019-02 within the last 3 Shorts. A trailer must keep the long video's topic, so it cannot be relabelled; it was marked failed (v-20261019-04). Options: Scout prefers long topics whose category is not in the last 3 Shorts on Studio days, or the owner decides whether trailers are exempt from the category window (variety.py is owner-only). A later Studio run can still make this trailer once credit_card leaves the window, if the one-trailer-per-long-video rule allows it.
